state_skeleton.title: The Skeleton of the Indian State
state_skeleton.subtitle: How India's Constitutional Machinery, Federal Tiers & Executive Committees Fit Together

core_principles.label: Sovereign Foundation
core_principles.detail: Written, supreme Constitution dividing power between Union & States (7th Schedule), anchored in Parliamentary Democracy (executive drawn from & responsible to Lok Sabha / Vidhan Sabha) and an Integrated Single Judiciary.

core_principles.label: Four Structural Distinctions UPSC Tests
core_principles.detail: (1) Constitutional (created directly by Articles) vs. Statutory (created by Parliamentary Act) vs. Executive/Non-Statutory (Cabinet Resolution) vs. Registered Society; (2) Constitutional safeguards vs. statutory tenure/salary parity; (3) Binding quasi-judicial decrees vs. purely recommendatory advice; (4) Exact Nodal Ministry.

core_principles.label: Nominal vs. Real Executive
core_principles.detail: All Union executive actions run in the name of the President (Art. 53/77), exercised on the binding aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (Art. 74), save narrow constitutional discretion.

union_organs_rows.head_and_composition: President + Rajya Sabha (max 250; current 245) + Lok Sabha (max 550; current 543)
union_organs_rows.key_responsibility: Union & Concurrent legislation, Budget/Money Bills (LS supremacy), Executive accountability via motions & Committees, Constitutional Amendment (Art. 368).

union_organs_rows.head_and_composition: President (titular head), Vice-President, PM + CoM (capped at 15% of LS via 91st Amend.), Cabinet Secretariat, PMO, All-India & Central Services
union_organs_rows.key_responsibility: Policy formulation, administration of Union Acts, defence & foreign affairs, appointments, ordinances (Art. 123), and executing Parliamentary laws.

union_organs_rows.head_and_composition: Single hierarchical pyramid: Supreme Court (CJI + max 33 Judges) → 25 High Courts → District & Subordinate Courts + Specialized Tribunals (Art. 323A/B)
union_organs_rows.key_responsibility: Constitutional interpretation, Judicial Review, Writ jurisdiction (Art. 32 SC / Art. 226 HC — wider for HC), Federal dispute resolution (Art. 131).

union_organs_rows.head_and_composition: CAG, ECI, UPSC/SPSC, Finance Commission, GST Council (279A), NCSC/NCST/NCBC, Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B)
union_organs_rows.key_responsibility: Insulated horizontal checks: free elections, public audit, merit civil services, fiscal federalism, and backward/minority safeguards.

union_organs_rows.articles: Parts VI, VIII, IX, IXA, IXB, X
union_organs_rows.head_and_composition: Governor + CM/CoM + State Legislature (bicameral in 6 States: UP, Bihar, MH, KA, AP, TS); Panchayats (243–243O), Municipalities (243P–ZG), 5th/6th Schedules
union_organs_rows.key_responsibility: State List governance, 29 Panchayat subjects (11th Schedule), 18 Municipal subjects (12th Schedule), Tribal Autonomous District Councils (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram).

schedule_summary.detail: Union List (List I: Defence, Foreign Affairs, Atomic Energy, RBI/Currency, Railways, Inter-State Trade); State List (List II: Police, Public Order, Public Health, Agriculture, Land); Concurrent List (List III: Education, Forests, Wildlife Protection, Criminal Law, Electricity). Residuary powers vest in Parliament (Art. 248).

Consolidated Fund of India (Art. 266(1) — withdrawal requires Parliamentary Appropriation Act; Charged expenditure non-votable); Public Account of India (Art. 266(2) — executive custody, no vote); Contingency Fund of India (Art. 267 — at disposal of President / Finance Secretary).
National Emergency (Art. 352 — war, external aggression, armed rebellion); President's Rule / State Emergency (Art. 356 — constitutional breakdown); Financial Emergency (Art. 360 — never imposed).

cabinet_committees.name: Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)
cabinet_committees.role: Approves senior civil, military, PSU & regulator appointments (Secretary+, Service Chiefs, RBI/SEBI senior picks).

cabinet_committees.name: Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS)
cabinet_committees.members: PM + Home, Defence, Finance & External Affairs Ministers
cabinet_committees.role: Highest executive body for national security, defence acquisitions, internal security & strategic foreign policy.

cabinet_committees.name: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)
cabinet_committees.role: Reviews economic trends, approves MSPs (based on CACP), PSU disinvestment, major infra projects & FDI proposals.

cabinet_committees.name: Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs (CCPA)
cabinet_committees.members: Senior Cabinet Ministers (PM is typically NOT a member!)
cabinet_committees.role: Schedules Parliament sessions, legislative agenda & government Bills; oversees floor strategy.

cabinet_committees.name: Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs (CCPA-Pol)
cabinet_committees.role: Resolves Centre-State & sensitive political/policy questions across ministries.

cabinet_committees.name: Cabinet Committee on Accommodation (CCA)
cabinet_committees.members: Senior Ministers incl. Housing & Urban Affairs
cabinet_committees.role: Allotment of government residences & accommodation policy.

cabinet_committees.name: CCIS & CCER (Investment/Growth & Employment/Skill)
cabinet_committees.members: PM + Finance, Commerce, Labour, Infra Ministers
cabinet_committees.role: Fast-tracks >Rs 1,000 Cr investments and skill/employment generation initiatives.

state_skeleton.skeleton_trap_note: UPSC Classic Trap: Cabinet Committees are EXTRA-CONSTITUTIONAL (established under Transaction of Business Rules, 1961 under Art. 77(3), NOT mentioned in the Constitution). The Prime Minister chairs most—EXCEPT Parliamentary Affairs and Accommodation (typically chaired by Home/Defence Minister)!

institutions.name: Parliament of India (Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha & Presiding Officers)

anchor.basis: Part V, Chapter II — Articles 79–122 (Art. 79: Parliament consists of President + Council of States [Rajya Sabha] + House of the People [Lok Sabha]).
anchor.key_amendments: 52nd Amend. (1985: 10th Schedule Anti-Defection); 91st Amend. (2003: removed 1/3rd split shield, 15% CoM cap); 104th Amend. (2020: ended 2 Anglo-Indian nominated LS seats); 106th Amend. (2023: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam — 33% women reservation in LS & State Assemblies post-Census/Delimitation, 15-yr sunset).
anchor.nodal_ministry: Independent Legislature (Floor coordination: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs; Independent LS & RS Secretariats under Speaker/Chairman)
anchor.established_year: 1952 (First elected Parliament after 1951–52 polls; Constituent Assembly acted 1947–52)
anchor.headquarters: Samvidhan Sadan / New Parliament House (Sansad Bhavan), New Delhi
anchor.essential_summary: India's supreme bicameral federal legislature exercising Union/Concurrent lawmaking, financial control over the Consolidated Fund, executive oversight, and constituent amending power (Art. 368).

composition.chairperson: Presiding Officers: Lok Sabha Speaker & Deputy Speaker (Art. 93 — elected by LS from among its members; Speaker does NOT vacate on LS dissolution until first meeting of new LS) | Rajya Sabha Chairman (VP ex-officio, Art. 64/89) & Deputy Chairman (elected by RS from among its members).
composition.members: Lok Sabha: Max 550 (530 States + 20 UTs; current strength 543; direct FPP election, 18+ suffrage). Rajya Sabha: Max 250 (238 State/UT elected via PR-STV by elected MLAs + 12 President-nominated for Art, Literature, Science & Social Service; current 245 = 233 + 12).
composition.eligibility_rules: Citizen of India; minimum age 25 yrs (LS) / 30 yrs (RS); registered voter in ANY parliamentary constituency (even for RS since 2003 RPA amend.!). Disqualifications: Art. 102 (Office of Profit, unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, non-citizen), RPA 1951 (2+ yr imprisonment = immediate disqualification per Lily Thomas 2013 + 6-yr post-release bar), & 10th Schedule (Defection).
composition.internal_wings: Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha Secretariats (Art. 98); Financial Committees (PAC, Estimates, COPU); 24 Departmentally Related Standing Committees (16 under LS Speaker + 8 under RS Chairman); House Committees (BAC, Rules, Privileges, Ethics); Whip system (not in Constitution—rooted in convention & 10th Sch.).

lifecycle.appointing_authority: Elected by People (LS) / Elected by State & UT MLAs + 12 Nominated by President (RS); Speaker/Deputy Speaker/RS Deputy Chair elected by simple majority of respective House.
lifecycle.selection_committee: Universal Adult Suffrage (LS); Indirect Open Ballot PR-STV by elected MLAs (RS — only Delhi, Puducherry & J&K UTs represented); 12 RS nominees by President on CoM advice.
lifecycle.selection_short: Direct Vote (LS) / MLA PR-STV + 12 Pres. Nominees (RS)
lifecycle.tenure: LS: 5 yrs (unless dissolved earlier; extendable 1 yr at a time during Art. 352) | RS: Permanent House (no dissolution; individual term 6 yrs, 1/3rd retire every 2 yrs)
lifecycle.age_limit: No upper retirement age ceiling (Min: 25 yrs LS / 30 yrs RS)
lifecycle.reappointment_and_post_retirement: Unlimited re-election permitted; Presiding Officers have no constitutional bar on further office.
lifecycle.reappointment_short: Unlimited re-election; no upper age cap
lifecycle.resignation_to: MPs resign to Speaker (LS) / Chairman (RS) [Art. 101(3) — presiding officer checks voluntariness!]. Speaker resigns to Deputy Speaker (& vice versa); RS Deputy Chair to Chairman.
lifecycle.removal_procedure: Speaker/Dy Speaker/Dy Chair: Resolution of respective House passed by EFFECTIVE MAJORITY (majority of all then members, 14 days' notice). RS Chairman (VP): Effective majority in RS + simple majority agreement in LS. Individual MP disqualification: President on ECI's binding opinion (Art. 103) OR Presiding Officer alone for 10th Schedule (subject to judicial review).
lifecycle.removal_short: Presiding Officers: Effective Majority (14d notice) | Defection: Speaker/Chair
lifecycle.funding_and_salary: Salaries of Presiding Officers (Speaker, Dy Speaker, Chairman, Dy Chairman) are CHARGED on Consolidated Fund of India (non-votable); MP salaries/allowances are voted by Parliament under Art. 106.

core_functions.label: Legislative & Constituent Supremacy
core_functions.text: Enacts laws on List I (Union), List III (Concurrent), residuary subjects (Art. 248), and List II under special triggers (Art. 249 RS 2/3rd resolution, Art. 250 Emergency, Art. 252 two+ States request, Art. 253 Treaties). Amends Constitution under Art. 368 (subject to Basic Structure).

core_functions.label: Financial & Budgetary Control
core_functions.text: No tax levied without law (Art. 265); no money drawn from Consolidated Fund without Appropriation Act (Art. 114). Lok Sabha holds decisive control over Money Bills & Demands for Grants (RS can only discuss, cannot vote on grants).

core_functions.label: Executive Accountability
core_functions.text: Council of Ministers is collectively responsible ONLY to Lok Sabha (Art. 75(3)). Controlled via Question Hour (Starred/Unstarred/Short Notice), Zero Hour (Indian innovation, non-statutory), Adjournment/Censure/No-Confidence Motions & Cut Motions (Policy, Economy, Token).

core_functions.label: Judicial & Electoral Functions
core_functions.text: Impeaches President (Art. 61 — 2/3rd total membership of each House), removes SC/HC Judges, CAG & CEC; participates in Presidential & Vice-Presidential elections.

mandate.power_nature: Supreme Legislative, Constituent, Financial & Executive-Oversight Sovereign Organ (subject to Basic Structure & Judicial Review).
mandate.special_powers: Lok Sabha Exclusives: Money Bills (Art. 110 — Speaker's certification final), No-Confidence Motion (min 50 MPs support, LS only), Discontinuing National Emergency (Art. 352), Joint Sitting presided by Speaker (Art. 118(4)). Rajya Sabha Exclusives: Art. 249 (legislate on State List by 2/3rd present & voting), Art. 312 (create new All-India Service by 2/3rd present & voting), initiating VP removal (Art. 67).
mandate.jurisdiction_limits_and_exclusions: Cannot alter Basic Structure (Kesavananda Bharati 1973); courts cannot inquire into internal procedural irregularities (Art. 122), yet substantive illegality/unconstitutionality & 10th Schedule Speaker orders ARE reviewable. Quorum = 1/10th of total strength of each House (incl. Presiding Officer). Max gap between two sessions = 6 months (Art. 85).
mandate.reporting_chain: Accountable to the electorate (LS); receives Annual Reports & Action Taken Memoranda from CAG, UPSC, ECI/Commissions & Ministers.
mandate.appellate_pathway: Constitutional validity of Acts & 10th Schedule Speaker rulings challenged via Writ Petitions before High Courts (Art. 226) or Supreme Court (Art. 32).

16 under Speaker + 8 under RS Chairman; scrutinizes Demands for Grants & Bills.
Allocates legislative floor time; Chaired ex-officio by Speaker (LS) / Chairman (RS).

genesis.founding_committee: Constituent Assembly of India (1946–1949); Parliamentary Committee framework modernized via Rules of Procedure (1952) & 1993 DRSC reform (expanded from 17 to 24 in 2004).

landmark_cases.label: Sita Soren v. UoI (March 2024, 7-Judge Bench)
landmark_cases.text: Unanimously OVERRULED P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998): MPs/MLAs enjoy NO immunity under Art. 105(2)/194(2) for accepting bribes to vote or speak—bribery offence completes upon acceptance.

landmark_cases.label: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992)
landmark_cases.text: Upheld 10th Schedule but subjected Presiding Officer's defection decision to judicial review on grounds of mala fides / perversity.

landmark_cases.label: Keisham Meghachandra Singh (2020)
landmark_cases.text: Directed Speakers to decide 10th Schedule disqualification petitions within a reasonable outer limit of 3 months absent exceptional circumstances.

common_traps.label: Lapsing of Bills on LS Dissolution (Art. 107)
common_traps.text: Bill pending in RS and NOT passed by LS does NOT lapse. Any Bill pending in LS (or passed by LS & pending in RS) LAPSES—EXCEPT pending Art. 108 Joint Sitting notice OR Bill returned by President for reconsideration!

common_traps.label: Effective Majority vs Special Majority
common_traps.text: Removing Speaker/Dy Speaker/Dy Chair requires EFFECTIVE majority (>50% of current strength excluding vacancies), NOT special 2/3rd majority.

common_traps.label: Speaker's Dual Casting vs First Vote
common_traps.text: Speaker does NOT vote in the first instance (exercises ONLY a casting vote on tie)—EXCEPT during a resolution for Speaker's own removal (votes in first instance, NO casting vote!).

common_traps.label: Minister Bar & RS Exclusion
common_traps.text: No Minister can sit on PAC, Estimates, COPU, or DRSCs. Estimates Committee has ZERO Rajya Sabha members.

rows: NO — can criticize/question, cannot topple govt
Exclusive intro + final say + votes on Demands for Grants
14-day advisory delay only; discusses Budget, no grant vote
Cannot initiate Art. 249 or Art. 312 resolutions

links.state_counterparts: State Legislatures (Art. 168–212): Unicameral in 22 States; Bicameral (Vidhan Sabha + Vidhan Parishad under Art. 169) in 6 States (UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana).
links.linked_acts_and_missions: Constitution Part V; RPA 1951; 10th Schedule; 104th & 106th Amendments; Parliamentary Committees (#6); President (#1); ECI (#21).

anchor.basis: Part XV, Articles 324–329 (permanent, independent constitutional body); statutory service rules under CEC & Other ECs Act, 2023.
anchor.key_amendments: 61st Amend. (1988): voting age 21→18; 1989/1993: permanently 3-member body; CEC & Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 replaced 1991 Act.
anchor.nodal_ministry: Independent (Administrative liaison: Ministry of Law & Justice, Legislative Dept.)
anchor.essential_summary: Superintends, directs, and controls electoral rolls and elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President, and Vice-President (NOT Panchayats/Municipalities).

composition.chairperson: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) — chairs Commission; holds equal voting weight with ECs (decisions by majority).
composition.members: CEC + such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may fix (currently 1 CEC + 2 ECs = 3 multi-member Commission).
composition.eligibility_rules: Under 2023 Act: persons holding or having held a post equivalent to Secretary to Govt of India, with integrity and knowledge/experience in management and conduct of elections.
composition.internal_wings: Deputy Election Commissioners (civil servants), Chief Electoral Officers (State level, IAS), District Election Officers, Returning Officers, and Electoral Registration Officers (under RPA 1950/1951).

lifecycle.appointing_authority: President of India (Art. 324(2) read with Sec. 6 of 2023 Act)
lifecycle.selection_committee: Under 2023 Act: PM (Chair) + Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha (or leader of largest opposition party) + 1 Union Cabinet Minister nominated by PM. Search Committee headed by Cabinet Secretary shortlists 5 names (Selection panel may look outside).
lifecycle.selection_short: PM + LoP (LS) + PM-nominated Union Minister (2023 Act)
lifecycle.reappointment_and_post_retirement: NOT eligible for reappointment under 2023 Act; if an EC is elevated to CEC, combined term cannot exceed 6 years. Constitution does NOT bar post-retirement govt appointments (classic trap!).
lifecycle.reappointment_short: Barred (max 6 yrs combined EC+CEC); post-ret. govt jobs not barred by Const.
lifecycle.resignation_to: President of India (writing under own hand)
lifecycle.removal_procedure: CEC: Removed ONLY like a Supreme Court Judge (Parliamentary special majority on proved misbehaviour/incapacity). Other ECs: Removed by President ONLY on the recommendation of the CEC.
lifecycle.removal_short: CEC: Like SC Judge | ECs: President only on CEC's recommendation
lifecycle.funding_and_salary: Under 2023 Act, salary/service conditions equal to Cabinet Secretary (downgraded from SC Judge parity under 1991 Act!). Conditions cannot be varied to disadvantage post-appointment. Election expenditure shared by Centre/States.

core_functions.label: Electoral Rolls & Constituencies
core_functions.text: Prepares and revises electoral rolls; notifies election schedules; grants/cancels recognition of National & State political parties and allots reserved symbols (Symbols Order, 1968).

core_functions.label: Model Code of Conduct (MCC)
core_functions.text: Enforces MCC from announcement of schedule until result declaration (MCC has no standalone statute; backed by IPC/BNS, RPA 1951 & ECI plenary Art. 324 powers).

core_functions.label: Advisory Disqualification Role
core_functions.text: Advises President (Art. 103) and Governor (Art. 192) on post-election MP/MLA disqualifications (binding advice!)—EXCEPT 10th Schedule defection (decided by Presiding Officer).

core_functions.label: Quasi-Judicial & Administrative
core_functions.text: Cancels/re-polls booths on rigging/booth capturing; derecognizes/suspends party recognition; advises President on Art. 356 extension beyond 1 year.

mandate.power_nature: Constitutional Plenary + Quasi-Judicial (binding advice under Art. 103/192; non-partisan dispute adjudication on party splits/symbols).
mandate.special_powers: Art. 324 acts as reservoir of plenary power where enacted law is silent (Mohinder Singh Gill case); state machinery deputed during polls comes under ECI disciplinary control.
mandate.jurisdiction_limits_and_exclusions: Does NOT conduct Panchayat or Municipal elections (vested in State Election Commissions under Art. 243K/243ZA). Cannot deregister a registered political party except in rare fraud/constitutional collapse cases. Art. 329 bars court interference mid-election (only Election Petition in High Court post-result).
mandate.reporting_chain: Independent; no annual Parliamentary report mandate in Art. 324 (issues statistical reports/compendiums).
mandate.appellate_pathway: Election disputes via Election Petition to High Court (RPA 1951) → Supreme Court. Party symbol orders (Para 15 Symbols Order) → Judicial review in HC/SC.

genesis.founding_committee: Constituent Assembly (Art. 324); Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) & Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms.

landmark_cases.label: Anoop Baranwal v. UoI (2023)
landmark_cases.text: 5-judge SC bench ordered interim Selection Panel (PM + LoP + CJI) until Parliament legislated—prompting Parliament to pass the 2023 Act replacing CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister.

landmark_cases.label: T.N. Seshan v. UoI (1995)
landmark_cases.text: Upheld equal status and voting weight of CEC and ECs; CEC is primus inter pares, not superior to ECs.

landmark_cases.label: ADR v. ECI (2024 — VVPAT)
landmark_cases.text: SC rejected 100% VVPAT verification / return to paper ballots, upholding EVM+VVPAT safeguards and 5% burned-memory verification option.

common_traps.label: Salary Downgrade Trap (2023 Act)
common_traps.text: CEC & ECs now get Cabinet Secretary equivalence (NOT Supreme Court Judge salary as under the repealed 1991 Act).

common_traps.label: CEC vs ECs Removal Trap
common_traps.text: Only CEC has SC-Judge-like Parliamentary removal security; other ECs can be removed by President solely on CEC's recommendation (not direct executive whim, yet no impeachment needed).

common_traps.label: Local Polls Trap
common_traps.text: ECI has ZERO role in Panchayat & Municipal elections; State Election Commission (SEC) is wholly independent of ECI, NOT a subordinate branch.

common_traps.label: Constitutional Silence Traps
common_traps.text: Constitution does NOT prescribe qualifications, exact tenure, or bar post-retirement govt employment for ECs—those details live in statute (2023 Act).

rows: President, VP, Parliament, State Assemblies & Councils
Governor of the State (conditions via State Legislature)
CEC: like SC Judge; ECs: on CEC recommendation
Like a High Court Judge (same manner & grounds)

links.state_counterparts: Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) at State level is ECI's administrative arm for Parliament/Assembly polls; State Election Commissioner (Art. 243K/243ZA) is an independent body solely for local bodies.
links.linked_acts_and_missions: RPA 1950 & RPA 1951; Delimitation Commission (#22); SVEEP; 61st & 84th Amendments (Reforms Book #7).

institutions.name: Reserve Bank of India, MPC & Payments Regulatory Board

anchor.basis: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (commenced 1 Apr 1935; nationalized 1 Jan 1949 via RBI Transfer to Public Ownership Act, 1948). Key regulatory authority also flows from Banking Regulation Act, 1949, FEMA 1999 & PSS Act, 2007.
anchor.key_amendments: Finance Act 2016 (inserted Sec. 45ZA–45ZO: Statutory Monetary Policy Committee & Flexible Inflation Targeting); Banking Regulation Amend. 2020 (brought Urban/Multi-State Co-op Banks under tighter RBI control); PSS Act Amend. / PRB Regulations (May 2025: replaced BPSS with 6-member Payments Regulatory Board).
anchor.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services — DFS) [Autonomy governed by RBI Act]
anchor.headquarters: Mumbai (shifted from Calcutta in 1937); 4 Local Boards (Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, New Delhi)
anchor.essential_summary: India's central bank and monetary authority governing price stability (4±2% CPI), currency issuance, banking/NBFC supervision, sovereign debt/forex management, and payment systems.

composition.chairperson: Governor of the RBI — full-time chief executive & ex-officio Chair of Central Board, MPC (with casting vote), and Payments Regulatory Board (PRB).
composition.members: Central Board of Directors (Sec. 8 — up to 21 members): 1 Governor + max 4 Deputy Governors (Official); 4 Directors nominated from 4 Local Boards + 10 Government-nominated Non-Official Directors + 2 Government Officials (usually Finance/DEA & DFS Secretaries).
composition.eligibility_rules: Governor/DGs appointed for whole-time service (no strict statutory degree bar, traditionally career central bankers/economists/senior civil servants). External MPC members must be persons of ability, integrity & standing in economics/banking/finance/monetary policy.
composition.internal_wings: Monetary Policy Committee (6 members, Sec. 45ZB); Payments Regulatory Board (6 members, May 2025); Board for Financial Supervision (BFS, est. 1994); 4 Local Boards (advisory); Financial Inclusion Fund / Ombudsman Scheme (Integrated Ombudsman 2021); Wholly owned subsidiaries: DICGC, BRBNMPL, ReBIT, IFTAS, RBIH.

lifecycle.appointing_authority: Central Government (recommended by FSIB / Search-cum-Selection & approved by ACC)
lifecycle.selection_committee: Governor/DGs: Cabinet Secretary-led Financial Sector Regulatory Appointment Search Committee (FSRASC) → ACC. External MPC Members: Search-cum-Selection Committee headed by Cabinet Secretary (incl. RBI Governor, DEA Sec., 3 experts).
lifecycle.selection_short: FSRASC / Cab. Sec. Search Panel → Central Govt (ACC)
lifecycle.tenure: Governor/DGs: up to 5 years (typically 3 yrs initially); External MPC: 4 yrs; Board Directors: 4 yrs
lifecycle.age_limit: Governor/DGs: no statutory age ceiling in RBI Act (administrative convention ~62/65); MPC external <70 convention
lifecycle.reappointment_and_post_retirement: Governor, Deputy Governors & Nominated Central Board Directors ARE eligible for reappointment/renomination. External MPC members are strictly NOT eligible for reappointment (Sec. 45ZD)!
lifecycle.reappointment_short: Gov/DGs eligible; External MPC members BARRED from reappointment
lifecycle.removal_procedure: Section 11: Central Govt may remove Governor, DG or Director at any time (with statutory grounds like unsoundness of mind, insolvency, moral turpitude conviction, or unexcused absence from 3+ consecutive Board meetings; Section 7 permits Govt policy directions in public interest after consulting Governor).
lifecycle.removal_short: Central Govt (Sec. 11 / Executive discretion; Sec. 7 policy directions)
lifecycle.funding_and_salary: Financially self-sustaining (seigniorage, open market interest, forex returns); surplus transferred annually to Govt of India (Bimal Jalan Economic Capital Framework). Salaries fixed by Central Govt.

core_functions.label: Monetary Policy & Inflation Targeting (Sec. 45ZA)
core_functions.text: Primary statutory objective: maintain price stability while keeping growth in mind. Target: 4% CPI (±2% band = 2%–6%), officially renewed for 5 years through March 31, 2031.

core_functions.label: Issuer of Currency (Sec. 22)
core_functions.text: Sole authority to issue banknotes (₹2 and above) under Minimum Reserve System (₹200 crore reserve: min ₹115 cr gold + ₹85 cr foreign securities). ₹1 note & all coins are issued by Ministry of Finance (Coinage Act 2011) and circulated via RBI.

core_functions.label: Regulator & Supervisor of Financial System
core_functions.text: Regulates Scheduled Commercial Banks, RRBs, Co-op Banks (BR Act 1949), NBFCs, CICs & All-India Financial Institutions (NABARD, SIDBI, NHB, EXIM, NaBFID). Enforces CRR, SLR, Basel norms & Prompt Corrective Action (PCA).

core_functions.label: Banker to Govt & Public Debt Manager
core_functions.text: Manages Consolidated Fund accounts, Ways & Means Advances (WMA), and Central/State sovereign bond auctions (G-Secs/T-Bills). Banker's Bank & Lender of Last Resort (LAF/MSF/SDF).

core_functions.label: Forex & Payment Systems
core_functions.text: Custodian of Foreign Exchange Reserves & FEMA 1999 manager; regulates UPI/RTGS/NEFT/IMPS & payment aggregators via the Payments Regulatory Board (2025).

mandate.power_nature: Statutory Monetary, Regulatory, Licensing & Penal Enforcement Authority (binding RBI Master Directions, monetary penalties, bank moratorium/reconstruction under Sec. 45 BR Act).
mandate.special_powers: Section 7(1) RBI Act: Central Govt can issue binding directions in public interest after consulting Governor. Integrated RBI Ombudsman Scheme merges Banking, NBFC & Digital Transactions Ombudsmen.
mandate.jurisdiction_limits_and_exclusions: Does NOT regulate: Stock/Derivatives markets & Mutual Funds (SEBI), Insurance (IRDAI), Pension Funds (PFRDA), GIFT City IFSC units (IFSCA), Housing finance registration was transferred from NHB to RBI in 2019 (while NHB continues refinance/supervision), and Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) outside BR Act banking.
mandate.reporting_chain: Submits Annual Report & Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India to Central Government (laid before Parliament); MPC publishes minutes 14 days post-meeting & Monetary Policy Report every 6 months.
mandate.appellate_pathway: Ombudsman orders → Deputy Governor (Appellate Authority); regulatory penalties/licensing appeals → Central Govt (specified sections) or High Court writ review.

Quorum = 4; 1 vote each + Governor has 2nd/CASTING vote on tie; external term 4 yrs, non-renewable; target 4±2% CPI through Mar 2031.
6 members: RBI Governor (Chair), DG Payments, ED Payments + 3 Central Govt nominees (DFS Sec., MeitY Sec., 1 expert)
Replaced older BPSS in 2025; RBI Principal Legal Adviser is permanent invitee; regulates UPI/card/settlement networks.
Sub-committee of Central Board: Governor (Chair), 4 DGs (incl. Vice-Chair DG) + 4 Central Board Directors
Consolidated supervision over commercial banks, NBFCs & urban co-op banks.
100% RBI-owned; chaired by RBI Deputy Governor
Insures bank deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (principal + interest combined); covers commercial, RRB & co-op banks.

genesis.founding_committee: Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926); Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended Flexible Inflation Targeting & MPC.

landmark_cases.label: IAMAI v. RBI (2020)
landmark_cases.text: SC set aside RBI's 2018 circular banning banks from servicing virtual currency exchanges on grounds of disproportionality (though upholding RBI's broad regulatory competence).

landmark_cases.label: Jayantilal N. Mistry (2015)
landmark_cases.text: SC held RBI is bound by RTI Act and cannot withhold bank inspection/defaulter data under fiduciary privilege.

common_traps.label: Constitutional vs Statutory Trap
common_traps.text: RBI is a STATUTORY body (RBI Act 1934), NOT a Constitutional body—nor was it originally govt-owned (started 1935 as private shareholders' bank, nationalized in 1949).

common_traps.label: ₹1 Note & Coins Trap
common_traps.text: ₹1 notes and ALL coins carry the Finance Secretary's signature and are issued by Ministry of Finance (Coinage Act 2011); RBI issues ₹2+ banknotes only.

common_traps.label: NPCI vs RBI Subsidiary Trap
common_traps.text: DICGC, BRBNMPL, ReBIT, IFTAS & RBIH are 100% RBI subsidiaries; NPCI (which runs UPI/RuPay) is NOT an RBI subsidiary—it is a Section 8 non-profit company promoted by RBI + IBA/banks.

common_traps.label: MPC Reappointment & Casting Vote
common_traps.text: Governor has a casting vote (NOT veto power!), and ONLY the 3 external MPC members are barred from reappointment (the Governor/DGs can be reappointed).

common_traps.label: GIFT City Exception
common_traps.text: Banking/financial units inside GIFT City IFSC are regulated by IFSCA (2019 Act), NOT directly by RBI/SEBI/IRDAI/PFRDA.

rows: Unified regulator for GIFT City IFSC (Banking+Markets+Insurance)

links.state_counterparts: None (Monetary policy & currency are strictly Union List entries 36 & 38); RBI operates 30+ Regional Offices across States/UTs.
links.linked_acts_and_missions: RBI Act 1934; Banking Regulation Act 1949; FEMA 1999; PSS Act 2007; FSDC (#50); SEBI (#45); IFSCA (#48); DICGC (#56); NPCI (#57); Jan Dhan / Digital Rupee (e₹) (Missions Book #3).

anchor.basis: National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 (Sec. 3); specialized fast-track quasi-judicial environmental tribunal (India became 3rd country globally after Australia & New Zealand to set up a green tribunal).
anchor.key_amendments: Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021 inserted Sec. 10A capping term at 4 yrs & minimum age 50—HOWEVER, SC in Madras Bar Association v. UoI (Nov 2025, 2025 INSC 1330) struck down 50-yr age floor, 4-yr truncation & 2-name SCSC panels, directing creation of a National Tribunals Commission.
anchor.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
anchor.headquarters: Principal Bench: New Delhi; 4 Regional Benches: Bhopal (Central), Pune (West), Kolkata (East), Chennai (South)
anchor.essential_summary: Adjudicates civil environmental disputes, compensation, and statutory appeals arising under 7 Schedule-I environmental laws based on Sustainable Development, Precautionary & Polluter Pays principles.

composition.chairperson: 1 Chairperson — must be a sitting or retired Judge of the Supreme Court of India OR Chief Justice of a High Court.
composition.members: Minimum 10 and Maximum 20 full-time Judicial Members + Minimum 10 and Maximum 20 full-time Expert Members (equal minimum/maximum parity!).
composition.eligibility_rules: Judicial Member: Judge of SC, or CJ/Judge of a High Court. Expert Member: Master's in Science/Engineering/Tech + 15 yrs experience (incl. 5 yrs practical env/pollution experience) OR 15 yrs administrative experience incl. 5 yrs handling environmental matters in Central/State Govt or national institution.
composition.internal_wings: Principal Bench (New Delhi) + 4 Zonal Benches (Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai); circuit benches held at Shimla, Shillong, Jodhpur & Kochi.

lifecycle.selection_committee: Chairperson: appointed by Central Govt in consultation with CJI. Judicial & Expert Members: appointed on recommendation of a Search-cum-Selection Committee (SCSC) constituted under NGT Rules (post-Nov 2025 SC ruling, must recommend 1 name per vacancy, not executive choice from 2 names).
lifecycle.selection_short: Chair: Consultation with CJI | Members: SCSC
lifecycle.tenure: 5 years (NGT Act); 2021 Act's 4-yr truncation invalidated by SC (Nov 2025)
lifecycle.age_limit: Chair: 70 yrs | Judicial (HC Judge): 67 yrs | Expert: 65/67 yrs
lifecycle.reappointment_and_post_retirement: Under NGT Act Sec. 7: Chairperson & Members are NOT eligible for reappointment (2021 Act tried allowing reappointment within 70/67 caps; check post-2025 tribunal bill). Barred from government employment & appearing before NGT for 2 years post-demitting office.
lifecycle.reappointment_short: Barred under NGT Act Sec. 7; 2-yr cooling-off bar
lifecycle.removal_procedure: Central Government may remove Chairperson or Judicial Member ONLY after an inquiry by a Judge of the Supreme Court (for proved misbehaviour/incapacity) in consultation with CJI. Expert Member removed by Central Govt on specified grounds after opportunity of hearing.
lifecycle.removal_short: Chair/Judicial: SC Judge inquiry + CJI consult | Expert: Central Govt
lifecycle.funding_and_salary: Charged through MoEFCC budgetary grants; salaries/allowances cannot be varied to disadvantage after appointment. Environmental Relief Fund receives Sec. 15/Public Liability compensation.

core_functions.label: Schedule I Exclusive 7-Act Jurisdiction
core_functions.text: Covers civil disputes & appeals ONLY under 7 enactments: (1) Water Act 1974, (2) Water Cess Act 1977, (3) Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, (4) Air Act 1981, (5) Environment (Protection) Act 1986, (6) Public Liability Insurance Act 1991, (7) Biological Diversity Act 2002.

core_functions.label: 3 Statutory Guiding Principles (Sec. 20)
core_functions.text: Must apply: (i) Principle of Sustainable Development, (ii) Precautionary Principle, and (iii) Polluter Pays Principle.

core_functions.label: Strict Statutory Filing Windows
core_functions.text: Sec. 14 (Original civil dispute): 6 months (+60 days grace); Sec. 15 (Compensation & restitution): 5 years (+60 days grace); Sec. 16 (Appellate against EC/SPCB/Forest orders): 30 days (+60 days grace). Disposal target: 6 months.

core_functions.label: Natural Justice Flexibility
core_functions.text: Not bound by strict procedural rules of Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) 1908 or Indian Evidence Act / Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam—guided by Principles of Natural Justice.

mandate.power_nature: Quasi-Judicial Binding Decree & Compensation Powers (orders are executable as decrees of a Civil Court; non-compliance punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to ₹10 crore!).
mandate.special_powers: Suo motu jurisdiction UPHELD by SC (Ankita Sinha 2021); possesses Civil Court powers for summoning, discovery & commissions; can award compensation, environmental restitution & impose heavy environmental damages.
mandate.jurisdiction_limits_and_exclusions: EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED FROM SCHEDULE I: (1) Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972; (2) Indian Forest Act, 1927; (3) Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006. Only civil cases involving 'substantial question relating to environment'—NO criminal trials.
mandate.reporting_chain: Decisions binding on parties/authorities; administrative oversight via MoEFCC (and proposed National Tribunals Commission per 2025 SC directive).
mandate.appellate_pathway: Direct appeal to Supreme Court of India within 90 days (Sec. 22). High Courts retain Art. 226/227 constitutional writ review (Madhya Pradesh HC Advocates Bar Assoc. v. UoI 2022).

genesis.founding_committee: 186th Report of the Law Commission of India (2003); Supreme Court directives in M.C. Mehta v. UoI & A.P. Pollution Control Board v. Prof. M.V. Nayudu.

landmark_cases.label: Municipal Corp. of Greater Mumbai v. Ankita Sinha (2021)
landmark_cases.text: SC held NGT holds suo motu powers to initiate environmental proceedings even without a formal petitioner.

landmark_cases.label: MP High Court Advocates Bar Assoc. v. UoI (2022)
landmark_cases.text: SC confirmed Sec. 22 direct appeal to SC does NOT oust High Courts' Art. 226/227 writ jurisdiction (Basic Structure).

landmark_cases.label: Madras Bar Association v. UoI (Nov 2025)
landmark_cases.text: Struck down 50-yr minimum age, 4-yr tenure cap & 2-name SCSC mandate under Tribunal Reforms Act 2021; directed establishing National Tribunals Commission.

common_traps.label: Excluded Forest & Wildlife Acts Trap (Classic!)
common_traps.text: NGT covers Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, NOT Indian Forest Act 1927, NOT Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972, and NOT Forest Rights Act 2006! (Can only intervene indirectly if a Schedule-I EPA/FCA violation overlaps.)

common_traps.label: CPC & Evidence Exemption Trap
common_traps.text: NGT has Civil Court powers (summoning, decree execution), yet is NOT bound by CPC 1908 procedure or Evidence rules—it follows Natural Justice.

common_traps.label: High Court Appeal Trap
common_traps.text: Statutory appeals under Sec. 22 go DIRECTLY to the Supreme Court (within 90 days), bypassing High Courts—yet HCs retain constitutional Art. 226 writ jurisdiction.

common_traps.label: Three Limitation Timers
common_traps.text: 6 months (Sec. 14 dispute) vs 5 years (Sec. 15 compensation) vs 30 days (Sec. 16 appeal)—each with max +60 days condonation!

rows: Retired SC Judge / HC Chief Justice

links.state_counterparts: None (No State Green Tribunals; NGT covers entire country through 1 Principal + 4 Zonal Benches).
links.linked_acts_and_missions: NGT Act 2010; EPA 1986; Water Act 1974; Air Act 1981; Forest Conservation Act 1980; Biological Diversity Act 2002; CPCB (#95); NBWL (#89); WCCB (#92).

anchor.basis: Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 — Chapter IVC (Sections 38Y & 38Z), inserted via 2006 Amendment (constituted 2007).
anchor.key_amendments: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 dropped legacy 'Tiger & Other Endangered Species' heading, aligned enforcement directly with CITES schedules & invasive alien species.
anchor.nodal_ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
anchor.headquarters: New Delhi (5 Regional Offices: Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Jabalpur + 3 Sub-Regional Offices: Guwahati, Amritsar, Cochin + 5 Border Units)
anchor.essential_summary: Statutory multi-disciplinary enforcement & intelligence bureau under MoEFCC mandated to combat organized domestic and trans-border wildlife crime and implement CITES enforcement.

composition.chairperson: Director of Wildlife Preservation (MoEFCC) serves ex-officio as Director, WCCB (NOT PM, NOT Env Minister!).
composition.members: Inspector-General of Police (Additional Director) + DIG of Police (Joint Director) + DIG of Forests + Assistant Directors / Wildlife Inspectors drawn from Police, Forest & Customs cadres.
composition.eligibility_rules: Multi-agency deputation combining All-India/Central Forest (IFoS), Police (IPS), and Customs/Revenue officers.
composition.internal_wings: Centralized Wildlife Crime Data Bank, 5 Regional Offices, 3 Sub-Regional Offices & 5 Border Units (incl. Indo-Nepal/Indo-Bangladesh/Northeast transit corridors).

lifecycle.selection_committee: Executive / Departmental deputation from Forest, Police & Customs services (no independent statutory Selection Panel).
lifecycle.selection_short: Central Govt departmental deputation (IFoS / IPS / Customs)
lifecycle.age_limit: Standard Central Govt service retirement (60 yrs)
lifecycle.reappointment_and_post_retirement: Standard Central deputation rules; no constitutional/statutory post-retirement bar.
lifecycle.removal_procedure: Repatriation / removal by Central Government under civil service deputation rules.
lifecycle.funding_and_salary: Budgetary grant under MoEFCC (Central Sector allocation).

core_functions.label: Central Crime Data Bank & Intel
core_functions.text: Collects, collates & disseminates wildlife crime intelligence to States/Police/Customs (Sec. 38Z).

core_functions.label: Inter-Agency & Border Coordination
core_functions.text: Coordinates State forest departments, Police, BSF/SSB/Customs at ports & borders; runs pan-India operations (e.g., Operation Kurma, Operation Clean Art, Operation Softgold, Operation Save Kurma).

core_functions.label: CITES & Foreign Assistance
core_functions.text: Implements international wildlife trade treaty obligations (CITES, Interpol Wildlife Crime Working Group, SAWEN) and assists foreign agencies.

core_functions.label: Capacity Building & Policy Advice
core_functions.text: Builds forensic/investigation capacity for States and advises Central/State Govts on wildlife crime policy & statutory amendments.

mandate.power_nature: Statutory Intelligence, Search, Seizure, Arrest & Prosecution Cognizance Agency.
mandate.special_powers: Under Sec. 38Z(2), exercises delegated WPA powers of entry, search, seizure, arrest & detention (Sec. 50(1)&(8)) and filing complaints/cognizance of offences (Sec. 55).
mandate.jurisdiction_limits_and_exclusions: Strictly wildlife offences under WPA 1972 & CITES customs interface—does NOT approve development/diversion clearances (that is NBWL/FAC) or manage tiger reserve funding/plans (NTCA).
mandate.reporting_chain: Reports administratively to MoEFCC (Director of Wildlife Preservation).
mandate.appellate_pathway: Prosecutions tried in designated Criminal/Magistrate Courts under WPA 1972 → Sessions / High Court.

genesis.founding_committee: Tiger Task Force (Sunita Narain Committee, 2005) after Sariska tiger extinction crisis recommended dedicated wildlife enforcement bureau + NTCA.

landmark_cases.label: UN Environment Award
landmark_cases.text: Awarded UNEP Asia Environmental Enforcement Award multiple times for Operation Save Kurma (turtles) & Operation Clean Art (mongoose hair).

common_traps.label: Ministry Trap
common_traps.text: WCCB sits under MoEFCC (NOT Ministry of Home Affairs, even though IPS/Police officers serve as Additional/Joint Directors!).

common_traps.label: Statutory Origin Trap
common_traps.text: Created by the 2006 Amendment to WPA 1972 (same amendment that made NTCA statutory—NOT an executive order and NOT under Forest Act 1927).

common_traps.label: Who Chairs WCCB
common_traps.text: Headed by the Director of Wildlife Preservation (ex-officio), whereas NBWL is chaired by the PM and NTCA & CZA are chaired by the Union Environment Minister.

rows: Wildlife crime intelligence, border enforcement & CITES coordination
Project Tiger governance, Tiger Reserve boundaries & funding
Apex wildlife policy & clearances inside National Parks/Sanctuaries
Recognition, standards & animal exchange for Indian Zoos

links.state_counterparts: State Wildlife Crime Cells / State Forest Vigilance Units (no separate State WCCBs; WCCB coordinates across States via 5 Regional Offices).
links.linked_acts_and_missions: WPA 1972 (2006 & 2022 Amendments); CITES; SAWEN; NTCA (#90); NBWL (#89); CZA (#91).

lifecycle_matrix.name: Parliament of India (Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha & Presiding Officers)
lifecycle_matrix.selection_committee: Direct Vote (LS) / MLA PR-STV + 12 Pres. Nominees (RS)
lifecycle_matrix.appointing_authority: Elected by People (LS) / Elected by State & UT MLAs + 12 Nominated by President (RS); Speaker/Deputy Speaker/RS Deputy Chair elected by simple majority of respective House.
lifecycle_matrix.tenure: LS: 5 yrs (unless dissolved earlier; extendable 1 yr at a time during Art. 352) | RS: Permanent House (no dissolution; individual term 6 yrs, 1/3rd retire every 2 yrs)
lifecycle_matrix.age_limit: No upper retirement age ceiling (Min: 25 yrs LS / 30 yrs RS)
lifecycle_matrix.removal: Presiding Officers: Effective Majority (14d notice) | Defection: Speaker/Chair
lifecycle_matrix.reappointment: Unlimited re-election; no upper age cap

lifecycle_matrix.name: Election Commission of India
lifecycle_matrix.selection_committee: PM + LoP (LS) + PM-nominated Union Minister (2023 Act)
lifecycle_matrix.appointing_authority: President of India (Art. 324(2) read with Sec. 6 of 2023 Act)
lifecycle_matrix.removal: CEC: Like SC Judge | ECs: President only on CEC's recommendation
lifecycle_matrix.reappointment: Barred (max 6 yrs combined EC+CEC); post-ret. govt jobs not barred by Const.

lifecycle_matrix.age_limit: Governor/DGs: no statutory age ceiling in RBI Act (administrative convention ~62/65); MPC external <70 convention

appellate_matrix.name: Parliament of India (Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha & Presiding Officers)
appellate_matrix.power_nature: Supreme Legislative, Constituent, Financial & Executive-Oversight Sovereign Organ (subject to Basic Structure & Judicial Review).
appellate_matrix.appellate_pathway: Constitutional validity of Acts & 10th Schedule Speaker rulings challenged via Writ Petitions before High Courts (Art. 226) or Supreme Court (Art. 32).
appellate_matrix.reporting_chain: Accountable to the electorate (LS); receives Annual Reports & Action Taken Memoranda from CAG, UPSC, ECI/Commissions & Ministers.

appellate_matrix.name: Election Commission of India
appellate_matrix.power_nature: Constitutional Plenary + Quasi-Judicial (binding advice under Art. 103/192; non-partisan dispute adjudication on party splits/symbols).
appellate_matrix.appellate_pathway: Election disputes via Election Petition to High Court (RPA 1951) → Supreme Court. Party symbol orders (Para 15 Symbols Order) → Judicial review in HC/SC.
appellate_matrix.reporting_chain: Independent; no annual Parliamentary report mandate in Art. 324 (issues statistical reports/compendiums).

appellate_matrix.name: Reserve Bank of India, MPC & Payments Regulatory Board
appellate_matrix.power_nature: Statutory Monetary, Regulatory, Licensing & Penal Enforcement Authority (binding RBI Master Directions, monetary penalties, bank moratorium/reconstruction under Sec. 45 BR Act).
appellate_matrix.appellate_pathway: Ombudsman orders → Deputy Governor (Appellate Authority); regulatory penalties/licensing appeals → Central Govt (specified sections) or High Court writ review.
appellate_matrix.reporting_chain: Submits Annual Report & Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India to Central Government (laid before Parliament); MPC publishes minutes 14 days post-meeting & Monetary Policy Report every 6 months.

appellate_matrix.name: National Green Tribunal
appellate_matrix.power_nature: Quasi-Judicial Binding Decree & Compensation Powers (orders are executable as decrees of a Civil Court; non-compliance punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to ₹10 crore!).
appellate_matrix.appellate_pathway: Direct appeal to Supreme Court of India within 90 days (Sec. 22). High Courts retain Art. 226/227 constitutional writ review (Madhya Pradesh HC Advocates Bar Assoc. v. UoI 2022).
appellate_matrix.reporting_chain: Decisions binding on parties/authorities; administrative oversight via MoEFCC (and proposed National Tribunals Commission per 2025 SC directive).

appellate_matrix.name: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau
appellate_matrix.power_nature: Statutory Intelligence, Search, Seizure, Arrest & Prosecution Cognizance Agency.
appellate_matrix.appellate_pathway: Prosecutions tried in designated Criminal/Magistrate Courts under WPA 1972 → Sessions / High Court.
appellate_matrix.reporting_chain: Reports administratively to MoEFCC (Director of Wildlife Preservation).
